target_in_paper: Section 14 (Dynamical Degrees of Rational Maps), Question 14.16.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the ambient object from the paper—a dominant rational self-map f : P^N dashrightarrow P^N—and the key unknown: whether there is an integer ell_f with 0 <= ell_f <= N controlling a finer growth law for the degree sequence deg(f^n). The trailing footnote marker '23' is also a strong clue that the intended target is exactly Question 14.16.
missing_details: The main omitted assertion is the actual growth formula: deg(f^n) ≍ n^(ell_f) delta_f^n.
The dynamical degree delta_f must be defined by delta_f := lim_{n->infty} (deg(f^n))^(1/n).
The notation ≍ must be unpacked exactly as in footnote 23: there exist constants c1, c2, c3 > 0 such that c1 F(n) <= G(n) <= c2 F(n) for all n >= c3.

A stand-alone version should specify the degree convention used in Section 14: f is represented by homogeneous coordinate polynomials of the same degree with common factors removed, and deg(f^n) is computed after the same normalization.
The question is posed for arbitrary N (implicitly N >= 1), not only for a fixed dimension chosen in advance.
The field of definition is left implicit in Section 14; a stand-alone wording should say that f is a dominant rational self-map of projective space over its field of definition.
No extra hypotheses such as morphism, algebraic stability, birationality, smoothness, or characteristic-0 assumptions belong to Question 14.16.
refined_question: Let N >= 1 and let f : P^N dashrightarrow P^N be a dominant rational self-map, written in homogeneous coordinates by polynomials of the same degree with common factors removed. Write deg(f^n) for the degree of the nth iterate defined in the same way, and let delta_f := lim_{n->infty} (deg(f^n))^(1/n) be the dynamical degree of f. Must there exist an integer ell_f with 0 <= ell_f <= N such that deg(f^n) ≍ n^(ell_f) delta_f^n; equivalently, are there constants c1, c2, c3 > 0, depending on f but not on n, for which c1 n^(ell_f) delta_f^n <= deg(f^n) <= c2 n^(ell_f) delta_f^n for all n >= c3?
justification: The draft is plainly aiming at the refined degree-growth problem in Section 14. The combination of a dominant rational map f : P^N dashrightarrow P^N, an integer ell_f with 0 <= ell_f <= N, and the stray footnote marker 23 uniquely matches Question 14.16. The nearby context explains why this question is asked: Definition 14.2 introduces delta_f as the exponential growth rate of deg(f^n), and the paragraph immediately before Question 14.16 notes that delta_f alone can miss an additional polynomial factor in the degree growth. To make the question stand alone and faithful to the paper, one has to restore the omitted asymptotic formula and define both delta_f and the notation ≍ exactly as the paper does.
